races.name: Malcolm Prescott 80th Birthday Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Albemagic
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just two starts showing a 2nd and 7th, both on similar going — the 8f second on good ground is the key piece of form here, though its natural inclination is to race closer to the pace rather than from the rear where the small field forces it; Clifford Lee takes over in the saddle and the Hollinshead yard has been quiet (0/3 in 14 days).

runners_data.name: Feliz Navidad
runners_data.note: Two runs both on good ground over 7-8f returning finishes of 5th and 5th suggest a horse that has yet to find its winning thread, but the O'Meara yard's current 5/43 strike rate over 14 days is a meaningful positive; David Nolan is an astute judge of pace who will use the prominent position well on a track where stalking the leader from second is a classically productive tactic.

runners_data.name: Asset
runners_data.note: The Sir Mark Prescott-trained three-year-old has four runs showing consistent placing (2-3-2-3) and is the only confirmed front-runner, which hands it full control of the race from stall to straight; the step back from 10f to 1m on Good to Firm is worth monitoring given two of its placed runs came at the longer trip, though the form on good-equivalent going (3 from 4 runs) is solid and Luke Morris rides with course authority.

races.paceDynamic: Asset is the lone confirmed front-runner in this three-horse field and will lead from the outset under Luke Morris, dictating every fraction on the Pontefract mile with no rival likely to challenge for the lead. Feliz Navidad will track prominently in second, meaning the race is essentially strung out from the front with both pace-setters filling the first two positions. Albemagic, redistributed to hold-up in the mapping, is not a natural closer by record but will find itself at the rear by default in so small a field — its two career runs show a prominent style that simply has no room to express itself here. The race shape strongly favours Asset as a front-runner who can control tempo without being pressured, and the Good to Firm ground at Pontefract rewards horses who travel sweetly in front rather than those required to make up ground from off the pace.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Asset Controls, Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Asset makes the lead unchallenged and sets a sustainable pace that suits its stamina profile on this mile.
scenarios.body: Asset dictates from the front with Luke Morris able to manage the fractions precisely, never over-extending on the Good to Firm ground; with only two rivals and no genuine pace threat, it faces no pressure until the straight where its three prior placed runs confirm it stays every yard of a mile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Feliz Navidad Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If Feliz Navidad travels comfortably on the pace and outbattles Asset in the final furlong with superior class.
scenarios.body: David Nolan is a polished race-reader who will sit a length behind Asset through the early stages and time a challenge into the straight, with David O'Meara's strong recent 5/43 trainer strike rate suggesting the horse is primed; Feliz Navidad's two runs over this trip and going combination give it the profile to quicken past a front-runner who has done all the work.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Albemagic Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final quarter-mile and Albemagic's hold-up position, forced by field size, becomes advantageous.
scenarios.body: Albemagic has shown ability at 8f on good ground and its lightly raced profile leaves a margin for improvement that Steph Hollinshead's runner may exploit; however, it is not a natural hold-up horse and depends on the front two setting an injudicious pace, which a canny handler like Sir Mark Prescott is unlikely to allow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Blanket Finish, All Three
scenarios.trigger: If Asset sets a genuinely slow early pace and the race turns into a sprint finish with margins compressed.
scenarios.body: A three-runner field on Good to Firm ground could theoretically see very slow early fractions that bunch the field together entering the straight; all three runners carry the same OR of 120 or similar ability levels, so a truly compressed finish is possible, though Asset's form of consistent placed runs suggests it handles varying pace well enough to resist.

watchPoints.text: Asset's solo pace-setting means the race is entirely in its hands — if Luke Morris misjudges fractions and sets an overly slow tempo, it sets up a sprint finish that could catch it out against the classier Feliz Navidad.

Feliz Navidad's two identical finishing positions of 5th suggest a horse that may have a habit of finding one too many lengths for comfort — watch whether David Nolan can position it aggressively enough to avoid a repeat.
Albemagic is racing off 29 days and switches jockeys to Clifford Lee; the Hollinshead yard's recent 0/3 in 14 days is a subdued form line worth noting before assuming improvement here.

The going is reported as Good to Firm at Pontefract throughout the card — all three runners have going tags of OK, but Asset's one Standfast run (GOO equivalent) and Albemagic's soft-ground 7th are the only minor going anomalies to monitor.

races.name: BYD Wakefield British EBF Stallion Studs Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Bolt Of Blue
runners_data.note: Finished fifth on debut over this C&D trip at Goodwood on Good ground, showing some ability; a natural hold-up horse whose Andrew Balding-like connections at Ed Dunlop suggest patience, but racing only 11 days on and forced closer than ideal by field composition, which tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Onslaught
runners_data.note: Richard & Fahey-trained two-year-old with form figures of 6-3 on Good ground at 5f-6f, showing a placing is within reach; runs out of a hold-up position naturally and will need the pace to be honest enough to peel late on good-to-firm going.

runners_data.name: Sole Ruler
runners_data.note: Paul Midgley runner with two runs at 5f-6f on Good, placing fourth and seventh; back after 35 days off which could mean a sharper preparation, though form figures suggest held by these rivals in similar conditions and style doesn't suit a slow-run race.

runners_data.name: The Mean Fiddler
runners_data.note: Debut runner for John & Sean Quinn with Jason Hart up and style entirely unknown; the complete absence of prior form is a genuine uncertainty, but the Quinn yard has a respectable 14-day strike rate and any natural early pace from this horse could prove transformative in a field lacking front-runners.

runners_data.name: Calef
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's consistent finisher with four runs all resulting in thirds and fourths on Good ground over 5f; a true hold-up horse who has been placed on the map in midfield due to field overcrowding at the rear, so should be assessed with that displacement in mind — place form is solid but a win remains elusive.

runners_data.name: Naval Cop
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's two-year-old with a sixth and a fourth over 5f-6f on Good, ridden by PJ McDonald; sits naturally at the back of the field but has been displaced to midfield on the map alongside other hold-up types, so his chance is contingent on a well-run race that simply may not materialise here.

runners_data.name: Shaqra Queen
runners_data.note: K R Burke debutant with Clifford Lee booked — Burke's 10 winners from 34 runners in the 14-day window is among the strongest trainer angles in this field; running style is completely unknown, but Burke's juveniles often arrive ready to perform and if she shows any early zip, she could shape the race entirely.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in the field and both The Mean Fiddler and Shaqra Queen making their debuts with unknown styles, this 5f Pontefract sprint is likely to develop into a slowly-assembled contest where no single horse dictates from the front with genuine authority. The bulk of the field — Bolt Of Blue, Onslaught, Sole Ruler, Calef, and Naval Cop — are all hold-up types by profile, meaning the early fractions are unlikely to be truly searching, and the race will compress into a sprint finish from the two-furlong pole. Three of those hold-up runners (Bolt Of Blue, Naval Cop, Calef) have been redistributed to midfield on the map because this field contains more genuine hold-up horses than there is rear-ground to accommodate, and in practice one or more will be forced to race closer than their natural style — but the most likely winner of a position at the head of affairs will come from one of the two unknown debutants, The Mean Fiddler or Shaqra Queen, should either show early speed. The tactical verdict is clear: this race shape favours horses with natural early pace to find a position uncontested, or those with the class to quicken through a tightly-grouped field late; pure hold-up horses will be disadvantaged by the lack of genuine pace to close into.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Debutant grabs rail, dictates
scenarios.trigger: If The Mean Fiddler or Shaqra Queen shows natural early speed and takes an uncontested lead through the opening furlong.
scenarios.body: With no proven front-runner in the field, either debutant could set a modest but controlled pace that plays to their own stamina and leaves the hold-up horses with insufficient time or space to pounce in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sprint finish, pack bunched
scenarios.trigger: If no horse establishes a clear lead and the field moves as a compressed group through the early stages.
scenarios.body: The resulting sprint from two furlongs out will be settled by raw speed and track position, favouring whichever runner finds a clean run from a handy midfield slot.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers finish fastest late
scenarios.trigger: If a moderate pace is set and the field fans wide in the straight, leaving clear daylight for runners to accelerate.
scenarios.body: Despite being mapped to midfield through redistribution, a horse like Onslaught or Sole Ruler who can produce a late burst may find enough room on good-to-firm ground where the surface rewards athleticism.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-up horse swoops late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and gaps open in the final furlong for a true come-from-behind finish.
scenarios.body: This is the least likely shape given the structural absence of any confirmed front-runner to generate real early fractions; Calef or Naval Cop would need an unusually fast-run race to produce a winning late run.

watchPoints.text: Shaqra Queen and The Mean Fiddler are the two unknown quantities — if either shows natural early pace in the first furlong, they could control this race from an uncontested lead with no genuine rivals likely to challenge them for the position.

Bolt Of Blue, Naval Cop, and Calef are all true hold-up horses that have been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding at the rear; watch whether any of them is actually ridden to race forward, as that would materially alter the race shape from what the map projects.

The going report consistently shows Good To Firm for this 5f contest despite the headline going being listed as Good — horses with form on faster ground, particularly Bolt Of Blue's positive Good-ground profile, may receive an unexpected surface advantage.

With seven runners and a potentially slow early pace, draw and early position could be decisive — watch for runners drawn wide who get shuffled back at the start and then face a wall of horses with no room to quicken in the final furlong.

races.name: Trevor Woods Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Coolree
runners_data.note: Progressive seven-year-old who has posted three top-four finishes at this trip on Good ground recently, wears a hood and tongue-tie, and P J McDonald's booking is a positive — a genuine pace-pressing type who is well-suited to sitting just behind a lone front-runner and kicking.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out, and a second three starts back, Coolree has been fairly consistent since a win six starts back. He returns within a week of that outing and has already raced over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Polygram
runners_data.note: Four-year-old hold-up performer who has been running over longer trips lately, stepping back to a mile here; Rowan Scott keeps things simple and the horse's three placed efforts on similar going are encouraging, though the drop back in distance and need to close from the rear are the key questions.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out, and third three starts back, Polygram rates the highest of this field on our figures but remains winless after six starts; the obvious question is whether she can finally get the job done.

runners_data.name: Mount King
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's six-year-old wears a tongue-tie and is a genuine sit-at-the-back type by nature, though the surfeit of hold-up horses in this field means he is unlikely to get the completely clear run from off the pace that he needs — his two wins on Good ground are a plus but his last five runs show a slide in form that tempers expectations.
runners_data.comment: Won last time out having managed nothing better than fifth in the five starts before that, Mount King has an obvious leap in form to confirm back over today's trip and going, with that being the main question mark.

runners_data.name: Stella Lucente
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner in the field, this three-year-old has a habit of finishing in the first three and wears a hood; Callum Rodriguez is an astute judge of pace and with no obvious challenger for the lead Stella Lucente holds a structural advantage that makes her the race's pivotal horse.
runners_data.comment: Stella Lucente has been a picture of consistency, following a string of places with a win last time out, and that progressive profile makes her our pick here. She has already raced over today's trip and looks sure to give another good account.

runners_data.name: Master of Entropy
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up type for John & Sean Quinn with Jason Hart booked; no win to his name and only a single placed effort on similar going, with his best effort coming over shorter, leaving him with plenty to prove at this level from the back of the field.
runners_data.comment: Master of Entropy's speed figures suggest more ability than his finishes have shown, with a fourth two starts back amid a middling sequence; he was only sixth last time out and needs to find more to trouble the principals here.

runners_data.name: The New Bay Pearl
runners_data.note: Simon Whitaker's four-year-old sits at the bottom of the handicap with OR 55 and is a true waiting-tactics horse in practice — though pressed into a midfield map slot by the crowded hold-up end of the field, she is unlikely to get the late-run scenario she needs, and Tom Eaves will struggle to manufacture momentum from the rear in a steadily-run race.
runners_data.comment: Fourth last time out, and fourth again two starts back, The New Bay Pearl has been well held in her other starts, and sits bottom of this field on our figures with little else to recommend her.

runners_data.name: Bradbury
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's three-year-old has form at much longer distances, so this mile trip represents a step back in trip; Billy Loughnane is an in-form claimer, the horse wears cheekpieces and a tongue-tie, and a recent sixth on Good ground from a prominent position is the most relevant piece, though the drop to a mile from staying tests his tactical speed.
runners_data.comment: Sixth last time out, having landed back-to-back wins two and three starts back, Bradbury needs to rediscover that spark; a modest speed figure adds to the case against him defying a lowly berth on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Stella Lucente is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace pressure coming from the rest of this seven-runner field, she is set to dictate from the outset at a controlled, sustainable gallop over Pontefract's flat mile on Good to Firm ground. Coolree and Bradbury will push for prominent positions just behind her, meaning the early order is relatively straightforward to establish, but the real pace battle is between those two for the lead group berths. The hold-up contingent — Polygram, Mount King, Master of Entropy, and The New Bay Pearl — will be ridden from further back, though Mount King and The New Bay Pearl are natural sit-and-wait types who have been redistributed forward on the map because the field carries more genuine hold-up horses than can all operate from their preferred rear position; of those, Polygram and Master of Entropy are most likely to actually slot into the rearward roles they want. A single uncontested front-runner controlling pace on fast ground at a flat track is a profile that historically rewards front-to-prominent runners who travel comfortably and finish strongly, making that style the clear beneficiary of this race shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Stella Lucente Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Stella Lucente bowls along in front at a honest but unforced tempo and the hold-up horses cannot close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Stella Lucente, in her natural role with Callum Rodriguez steering, sets a measured pace that suits her front-running profile and simply outstays rivals over the final two furlongs; Coolree and Bradbury, sitting close and travelling well, are ideally placed to pick up any scraps if she ties up.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Swamp Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Coolree and Bradbury push hard enough to force a pressured pace, softening Stella Lucente and setting things up for a late challenge.
scenarios.body: Stella Lucente is drawn into a faster-than-ideal gallop by the prominent duo, leaving her vulnerable in the closing stages as her stamina gets tested on the quick ground; Coolree, with strong Pontefract form at this distance, is best placed to capitalise as one who could press and then quicken.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the final two furlongs after a hot early tempo and the hold-up horses find enough room to finish through.
scenarios.body: Polygram is the most naturally suited of the hold-up brigade to this scenario, having placed on similar ground and distance combinations, and could emerge from behind if the race is truly run to suit closers; Master of Entropy lacks a win on the board at this level but holds each-way claims if the shape opens up late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Chaos, Field Splits
scenarios.trigger: If a tardy start or interference scrambles positions and the race is run in sections, negating the advantage of Stella Lucente's lone-leader profile.
scenarios.body: In this unlikely scenario the redistribution of Mount King and The New Bay Pearl into midfield becomes genuinely relevant as they race closer than ideal to their preferred rear stations, but their STYLE_FIT discounts make a winning impact improbable; Coolree's versatile prominent style gives her the best chance of adapting if the shape falls apart entirely.

watchPoints.text: Stella Lucente is the axis of this race — if she is allowed to bowl along at a comfortable, uncontested tempo, the race is almost entirely run on her terms and every other runner is chasing a moving target.

Coolree's draw and P J McDonald's tendency to press from the front means she could push Stella Lucente into a faster-than-ideal pace; watch the early fractions to see whether the two lock horns or whether McDonald settles for second.
Polygram's trip has been 10f-12f in recent starts — if the mile comes too sharp and he cannot sustain a finishing run on fast ground, his place claims evaporate quickly in a small field.

Mount King and The New Bay Pearl are both natural hold-up horses forced into a more prominent position by field dynamics; if the pace is genuine and the field strings out, neither may find the clear passage they need to make their finishing effort count.

The going report consistently reads Good to Firm across all times at Pontefract today — any horse with a CONCERN on fast ground should be monitored at the start, and Stella Lucente's hood and front-running style means her behaviour in the early stages is worth watching closely.

races.name: William Hill Pomfret Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's consistent performer arrives 15 days fresh with strong similar-going form (13/15 runs), but by nature wants to race prominently — in a field already stacked with front-runners, he is likely to be shuffled wider than ideal and forced to work harder than his best form demands.|
runners_data.comment: A solid second three starts back, Cerulean Bay has since faded to fifth and eighth, including last time out; he still rates within a few pounds of the leading pair, so a return closer to that level would make him a leading threat.

runners_data.name: Holloway Boy
runners_data.note: K. R. Burke's six-year-old is a confirmed front-runner whose trainer is 10/34 in a 14-day window; he has posted nine placed efforts at 1m on Good in recent history and carries his rating well, but has been unable to convert when leading — the question is whether rivals can close him down before the line.|
runners_data.comment: Holloway Boy has been admirably consistent - runner-up last time out, and again three and five starts back - and rates the best of these, with the yard in good order lately (10 from its last 34); turning those places into a win remains the only miss.

runners_data.name: Point Lynas
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's seven-year-old gelding returns after a 73-day break wearing headgear and has placed twice at 1m on Good going in recent form, suggesting the trip and surface suit; the longer absence is the key risk, though Bethell runners often run well fresh and Callum Rodriguez keeps the ride.|
runners_data.comment: Point Lynas rates only narrowly behind the selection on our figures, having been a fair fourth last time out, but a 73-day absence and a moderate sequence before that - ninth, seventh and sixth - are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse whose recent form includes a return to 1m after a foray over longer trips, but only one placed run in 15 outings on similar going is a significant concern; Ben Haslam's charge will need a genuinely strong pace to get involved and that looks unlikely in this race shape.|
runners_data.comment: Crystal Flyer bounced back to be runner-up last time out having been well beaten in the race before, and that improved effort is the most encouraging piece of recent form on show; the query is whether she can repeat it given modest efforts further back.

runners_data.name: Model Yuko
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old has winning form at 1m on Stanmore going and placed form on Good, but steps back from 10f+ in recent starts — naturally a hold-up type, he is also redistributed by the race shape into a midfield slot that is not fully his own, compounding the challenge.|
runners_data.comment: Model Yuko has finished no better than seventh in her last two starts, a marked fall from a win four starts back, and a third five starts back; she rates bottom of these on our figures and needs to rediscover that level to feature.

runners_data.name: Mostar Dreams
runners_data.note: Adrian Keatley's five-year-old has two wins and strong placed form but most of that was on Stanmore and Good-to-Firm Irish tracks; his hold-up style needs pace to aim at, and the controlled fractions Holloway Boy is likely to set will blunt his finishing effort.|
runners_data.comment: Mostar Dreams was a fair fourth last time out, and a close second two starts back, though a well-beaten ninth three starts back shows the inconsistency that leaves her the outsider of these on our figures.

races.paceDynamic: Holloway Boy is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure him, he is highly likely to dictate from the front at a controlled, sustainable tempo on this Good to Firm mile at Pontefract. Cerulean Bay and Point Lynas are both naturally prominent types who will look to track closely, meaning the early order could be tighter than the lone leader tag implies, but neither is likely to force Holloway Boy into a truly contested gallop. The field contains more prominent types than the race shape can naturally accommodate — Cerulean Bay and Model Yuko are redistributed away from their preferred positions, with Holloway Boy and Point Lynas most likely to physically secure the lead and the rails respectively. A controlled pace set by Holloway Boy on fast ground at Pontefract's turning mile favours a prominent or tracking racer who can conserve energy early and sustain a kick into the straight, rather than a pure hold-up type waiting for a strong pace that may never materialise.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Holloway Boy Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Holloway Boy secures the lead unchallenged and dictates a comfortable tempo throughout the mile.
scenarios.body: Holloway Boy sets honest but not brutal fractions, the field strings out on the turn, and his rivals lack the finishing kick to reel him in on fast ground; Point Lynas, who has consistently placed from a tracking position at this trip in similar going, is best positioned to mount a challenge.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Holloway Boy's lead is tracked closely by Cerulean Bay or Point Lynas and the leader ties up inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The pace is sufficiently honest to expose Holloway Boy in the closing stages, and a horse travelling smoothly just off the shoulder delivers the winning thrust; Point Lynas's consistent placed form at 1m on Good ground makes him the most credible beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Storms Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to open a gap for a late finisher and the hold-up runners find a clear run.
scenarios.body: Crystal Flyer or Mostar Dreams would need fractions much stronger than Holloway Boy is likely to set, making this scenario materially less probable; Mostar Dreams has winning form at the trip on similar ground and would be best placed of the closers if a gap opens late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Pace Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If multiple prominent types jostle for position early, disrupting Holloway Boy's rhythm and creating an uneven gallop.
scenarios.body: A scrambled early order could produce a falsely run race that benefits a fresh-legged horse coming from off the pace with a late surge; Model Yuko, dropped back in trip and trained by Roger Varian, holds latent form but is racing out of natural role throughout.

watchPoints.text: Holloway Boy's strike rate of 0 wins from 9 prominent runs is a red flag for punters expecting him to convert his front-running position — watch whether he is challenged off the bridle before the turn.|

Point Lynas returns after 73 days off for Edward Bethell and is wearing headgear; watch his early behaviour and how smoothly he settles behind the leader, as a fresh horse in Listed company can either sparkle or bubble.|

Cerulean Bay is forced out of his natural prominent berth by the race shape — watch whether David Nolan elects to push forward regardless and whether that move disrupts Holloway Boy's rhythm in the early exchanges.|

Model Yuko steps sharply back in trip from 10f to 1m for Roger Varian — watch how he travels through the first half of the race; if he is already off the bridle entering the back straight, his chance is effectively gone in a slowly-run race.|

races.name: Pontefract And District Golf Club Ltd Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: O'Meara's four-year-old is 12/14 in similar going conditions and owns a course win, making this Good to Firm Pontefract track well-suited; the sole confirmed front-runner in the race, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a reminder its chance hinges on holding that lead rather than being pressed into a fight.|
runners_data.comment: Percy's Daydream has won twice in her last six starts, most recently three starts back, and returns quickly after just nine days; modest fourths in her last two starts are the only blot, but she rates the best of these on our figures.

runners_data.name: Without Compromise
runners_data.note: 128 days off the track for Brittain's five-year-old is a significant fitness concern, and its entire recent form history reads across Southwell's standard surface — the move to turf in Good to Firm conditions represents an unproven dimension, compounding the layoff worry.|
runners_data.comment: Without Compromise won four starts back, with thirds either side of that (two starts back, and five starts back), so the engine remains sound on our figures; a 128-day absence and a well-beaten eighth last time out are the obvious concerns.

runners_data.name: Pomme Pomme
runners_data.note: Channon's filly brings an apprentice claimer in Rose Dawes (5lb claim) which may offset the OR disadvantage, but the horse's most productive form has come on Good and Good to Soft ground with a couple of placed efforts over similar trips; a true hold-up operator who needs the race run to suit.|
runners_data.comment: Pomme Pomme rates the outsider of this five on our figures, undone by ninth two starts back, and no better than fifth last time out; a second three starts back, and a third five starts back, show she does have ability on her day.

runners_data.name: Jez Bomb
runners_data.note: Sam England's five-year-old arrives on the back of back-to-back wins and carries the highest recent momentum in the race — a prominent runner who should slot comfortably just behind the leader, with headgear (p) worn again suggesting a settled profile and the Good-ground form (8/15) workable.|
runners_data.comment: Jez Bomb has followed a win two starts back with a second last time out, giving him solid claims among the dangers here; the query is reconciling that with a spell of ninth, fourth and unplaced efforts further back.

runners_data.name: Moonjid
runners_data.note: Appleby's four-year-old is a legitimate prominent racer who owns a 10f Pontefract win in its last five outings; however, with Percy's Daydream and Jez Bomb filling the forward slots, De Sousa will be forced to settle further back than the horse prefers, reducing the chance that its natural aggressive style can be deployed.|
runners_data.comment: Moonjid won two starts back, and was third three starts back, putting him among the dangers here; but the yard is currently out of form (no winners from its last 22 runners) and he was only seventh when last seen.

races.paceDynamic: Percy's Daydream is the confirmed front-runner here and, with only Jez Bomb as a genuine second prominent type, faces minimal pressure for the lead over this 1m2f trip on Good to Firm ground at Pontefract. Percy's Daydream can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop, denying rivals the scrappy pace that would stretch them out and instead setting up a test that rewards those who travel well within themselves. Moonjid is a natural prominent racer who cannot secure their preferred position given Percy's Daydream and Jez Bomb already filling those slots — they have been mapped to midfield accordingly. This race shape firmly favours front-running and prominent profiles who can dictate or sit just off an uncontested leader, with hold-up horses Without Compromise and Pomme Pomme needing an honest pace to generate the late momentum their styles demand — a pace that may simply never materialise here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Daydream Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream leads uncontested and sets a measured, front-running tempo that suits the leaders.
scenarios.body: Percy's Daydream dictates the fractions from the front, with Jez Bomb sitting a length or two behind in a comfortable rhythm that denies the hold-up horses any real pace to chase; the leader's Good to Firm record (12/14 in similar going) and O'Meara's current form underpin this shape as comfortably the most likely outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Jez Bomb Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream sets a genuine pace and Jez Bomb, tracking throughout, produces a decisive late surge to overhaul the leader.
scenarios.body: Jez Bomb's recent back-to-back wins over shorter give it the tactical speed to sit close to the pace and strike when the leader tires; the horse's Good-ground form (8/15 but productive) and proven winning ability at the right moment make this a credible second shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Capitalise Late
scenarios.trigger: If Percy's Daydream sets an unexpectedly strong pace that begins to unwind the field in the final two furlongs, allowing hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: Pomme Pomme has solid place form in Good ground and Cam Hardie gets Without Compromise for the first time after a long absence — both need the race to fall apart in front of them; this scenario depends on a pace injection that current race dynamics make unlikely given the small, largely hold-up field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Scrapper Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Moonjid, unable to secure a prominent berth, settles in midfield and benefits from a pace collapse that brings the whole field together.
scenarios.body: Moonjid has winning form at this level and De Sousa is capable of conjuring an unexpected run, but the horse is a genuine prominent racer forced out of role, making this outcome structurally the least likely in this configuration.

watchPoints.text: Percy's Daydream leads without a meaningful challenger — if Mark Winn dictates an uncontested crawl, hold-up horses Without Compromise and Pomme Pomme may simply never get into the race.

Without Compromise's 128-day layoff combined with a switch from Southwell standard to Good to Firm turf creates a dual-risk profile — Cam Hardie will need the horse to show immediate readiness to be competitive.

Moonjid is forced out of its natural prominent role by the presence of two other forward-going types — watch whether De Sousa attempts to push forward early and disrupt the anticipated running order at the start.

Jez Bomb steps back up to 1m2f after two wins at shorter — the trip extension is the one question mark for a horse whose recent momentum is the strongest in the field; how it handles the extra distance will define its finishing effort.|

races.name: Roy Winstanley Memorial Raising Encephalitis Awareness Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Starsong
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner and likely to set a comfortable solo lead on Good to Firm; Michael Appleby's string is out of form (0/22 over 14 days) and five recent placings in a row suggest Starsong runs to a ceiling without winning — the lead role is real but the finishing cut may be lacking.
runners_data.comment: Frames without landing the win - a third four starts back her best of six - and quick to reappear just eight days on, with today's trip and going already covered. The main risk is a yard without a success in its last 22 (0% in a fortnight).

runners_data.name: Bullington Bry
runners_data.note: Jessica Macey returns one winner from five in the last fortnight, and this four-year-old's best recent form is a second over 6f on Good ground — the closest surface match in the field; prominent style suits the expected pace shape perfectly and Lewis Edmunds can slot in just off Starsong.
runners_data.comment: Runner-up last time out and already has run over today's trip and going, he carries 134 lb from draw 11; the downside is he was no better than seventh in three of his other five recent starts and remains winless in that spell.

runners_data.name: Rain Cap
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old veteran with strong Good-ground placed form over this exact trip, including a win at 6f on similar surfaces; prominent style is ideal for the anticipated shape and Sean Kirrane keeps it simple — this horse is tactically uncomplicated and could outrun its odds quietly.
runners_data.comment: A third four starts back, and a second five back, hint at scope, but he has since faded to fifth last time out, and fourth two starts back. Already race-experienced over today's trip and going, he rates just a midfield player here.

runners_data.name: Go Victor
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a worrying recent form string of three zeros and a fade-in-finish flag; hold-up style on a track and in a race shape that does not favour late closers makes this a difficult proposition, and Paul Mulrennan will struggle to find daylight off a modest pace.
runners_data.comment: A useful 55 official rating and a solid speed figure of 59 hint at more within him than recent finishing positions suggest, with today's trip and going already banked as experience. The finishes have been modest of late, but 23 days off should freshen him for this.

runners_data.name: Eldeyaar
runners_data.note: Has won and placed at this trip on Good ground and represents genuine ability, but is a true hold-up specialist whose position is compressed into midfield by the sheer number of backmarkers in this field — Cam Hardie will need fortune in running that the race shape may not provide.
runners_data.comment: A winner four starts back, and a third both two and three starts back, he's shown solid recent form. The concern is a below-par eighth last time out following a 52-day absence, though he has already raced over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: Miss Magic Dragon
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Good ground in recent form and Clifford Lee is capable of conjuring a prominent pitch if needed; hold-up tag is honest but the three-year-old has the profile to be competitive if she gets a clear run down the rail in the closing stages.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, though form has since eased to midfield finishes and a modest speed figure last time. She has already raced over today's distance, but sits only in mid-pack on our figures here.

runners_data.name: Battenburg Belle
runners_data.note: Consistent place-getter over 6f on Good and Good to Firm ground — five placings from nine recent starts tells its own story; Jason Hart has the experience to position her optimally just off the pace, and with no fade flag her finishing effort looks reliable in this company.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back, and second in three of her runs before that, she has been the model of consistency this term. A below-par fifth last time out is the one blot, though today's trip and going hold no fears.

runners_data.name: Summer Rain
runners_data.note: True hold-up type pushed into the midfield representation due to field congestion, and the form figures of 9-5-9-5-13 over the last five runs paint a picture of a horse that rarely threatens; Good-ground record produces no wins or places, and the redistribution effect compounds an already modest profile.
runners_data.comment: Well held in all five of his recent starts, with two ninths among them and never better than fifth, he sits bottom of our figures here. The one plus is a useful speed figure of 59 last time, and he already has experience over today's trip and going.

runners_data.name: My Boy Jack
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old whose natural style is hold-up but is mapped closer than he would naturally race given the backfield volume; Mason Paetel claims 5lb which helps with the weight, but the recent form string of 7-4-5-0-3 over trips longer than today's suggests the drop to 6f is untested territory relative to his best efforts.
runners_data.comment: Consistently in and around the frame - fourth last time out, and third two starts back - he already has experience over today's trip and going, though has yet to finish inside the first two in six attempts. Our figures rate him a shade above his current mark.

runners_data.name: Coiled
runners_data.note: Carries a fade-in-finish warning alongside a redistributed tag — a doubly unfavourable combination; Silvestre De Sousa is a high-class booking but even he cannot fully compensate for a horse whose 12-of-15 Good-ground outings all on this surface have produced no wins and whose recent form reads 0-0 across the last two starts.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten in each of his last five starts, with successive unplaced efforts his most recent form, he is understandably towards the foot of these rankings. He does already have experience over today's trip and going, for what encouragement that offers.

runners_data.name: Power Of Chora
runners_data.note: Joey Ramsden-trained three-year-old whose best results have come at 5f on Good ground rather than 6f, and who is a genuine hold-up horse placed into midfield by the field's structural crowding at the rear; Taryn Langley's 5lb claim is useful but the step up in trip and out-of-role positioning make this a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back is the highlight among mostly one-paced efforts, with three eighth-place finishes dotted through her recent starts. She already has today's trip and going covered, and a useful speed figure of 56 last time keeps her in the mid-table mix here.

races.paceDynamic: Starsong is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner 6f handicap and, crucially, faces no genuine rival for the lead — Bullington Bry and Rain Cap are prominent types but neither is likely to throw down an early speed duel, meaning Starsong can slide into an uncontested, comfortable rhythm on Good to Firm ground. That controlled, single-pacesetter dynamic keeps the tempo honest but not truly searching, which historically at Pontefract's straight 6f compresses the field and makes it difficult for pure hold-up horses to generate the momentum they need from off the pace. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than can realistically occupy their natural position: Power Of Chora, Eldeyaar, Summer Rain, My Boy Jack and Coiled are all true hold-up horses shuffled into the midfield representation on the map, meaning the rear of this race is genuinely congested with animals racing out of role. The race shape therefore favours prominent racers who can travel just behind Starsong and quicken through the final two furlongs — horses with a positive, handy profile are most advantaged here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Starsong Leads, Prominents Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Starsong dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the horses travelling just behind produce the decisive move turning for home.
scenarios.body: Starsong's uncontested lead sets a manageable pace and the prominent pair of Bullington Bry and Rain Cap, already on her heels, have the shortest distance to cover when the race begins in earnest; on Good to Firm ground at Pontefract that front-two-lengths advantage is rarely overcome by late finishers over 6f. Battenburg Belle, who has run five places from the front before, could also be positioned close enough to land the telling blow from a slightly more patient angle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Battenburg Belle Delivers Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely steady enough that one hold-up horse — running true to style — can produce a clean, angled run to the stands rail in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Battenburg Belle has a strong record at this trip on Good ground, has placed at this level before, and Jason Hart will be well aware of the compressed pace map; if she gets a clean passage she has the proven finishing kick to reel in a moderate gallop-setter. Unlike many in this field she is a genuine hold-up horse whose style is not compromised by redistribution, giving her a legitimate late-race threat.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Quickens, Starsong Stretched
scenarios.trigger: If Bullington Bry or Rain Cap push forward early and force a genuinely fast early split that tests Starsong's stamina into the final furlong.
scenarios.body: A contested early pace would expose Starsong, whose recent form shows a cluster of fifth-place finishes and whose trainer has a blank 14-day strike rate, and horses with stamina reserves — particularly Rain Cap who has course-and-distance placed form — would benefit as rivals tire.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Cavalry Fails to Fire
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is modest, the race bunches into the final furlong and the backmarkers — most of whom are racing out of their natural role — cannot generate sufficient momentum to peg back the leaders.
scenarios.body: With Power Of Chora, Summer Rain, Coiled and My Boy Jack all true hold-up types crowded in midfield and forced wide or blocked late, they collectively underperform while the prominently-placed runners dominate the finish; this is the scenario that exposes the field's structural overcrowding at the rear.

watchPoints.text: Battenburg Belle is the most dangerous hold-up horse in the race — Jason Hart will be watching for a gap on the stands rail, and if the pace is even marginally soft in the middle stages she has the form to swoop late on this ground.

Bullington Bry and Rain Cap are both genuine prominent types who could push forward early and inadvertently create a contested pace — if they both press Starsong hard before halfway, the expected controlled tempo disappears and the race shape changes entirely.

The cluster of five redistributed hold-up horses (Power Of Chora, Eldeyaar, Summer Rain, My Boy Jack, Coiled) creates significant traffic risk in the final two furlongs — watch for interference and blocked runs as they all seek the same limited space late.

Starsong's trainer Michael Appleby has sent out 0 winners from 22 runners in the last 14 days — note whether Starsong travels comfortably in the lead or begins to idle once clear, as any sign of idling could allow the second wave to swallow her.

Going confirmed as Good to Firm for this race despite the card header showing Good — any horse with a going preference for softer conditions (Bullington Bry has softer-ground form, Summer Rain has no wins on Good) may find conditions less forgiving than their connections hope.

races.name: Sarah Gusterson Memorial Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with two wins and three places in similar going over 5-6f, trained by Sam England who is in good form at 2 from 14 over the past fortnight; ran just one day ago so fitness is not a concern, but the hold-up style is a tactical risk against an uncontested front-runner.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back, and again four starts back, with minor-placed efforts either side, he is quick to reappear just a day after his latest run and rates comfortably clear of this five-runner field. He has already run over today's trip and going and is the one to beat.

runners_data.name: Bell Shot
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old veteran wearing a visor, proven hold-up type whose recent form has come over 7f-8f — the drop back to 6f is a query, and apprentice Mason Paetel (5) riding adds a further degree of uncertainty against more experienced handlers in a race dominated by pace control.
runners_data.comment: A third two starts back, and again four starts back, with a fourth last time out, he is quick to reappear just eight days on and already knows today's trip and going. The worry is a stable running at 0% from its last 22 in the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Goyard
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner for David O'Meara who gets to lead uncontested here; best form is over 5f (one win) and this 6f trip is a slight stretch, which is the main vulnerability, though the STYLE_FIT flag is low-concern given they naturally take up the prominent role rather than racing out of it.
runners_data.comment: A winner five starts back, and third two starts back, point to real claims, with today's trip and going already banked. The danger is finding one too many on his day, with two eighth-place efforts - including last time out - among his five recent starts.

runners_data.name: The Good Biscuit
runners_data.note: Ruth Carr's five-year-old has sound course-and-distance form — five of the last five runs on Good over 6f — and is prominent enough to sit on Goyard's shoulder without burning too much fuel; the 3 from 17 trainer strike rate over 14 days is modest but Jason Hart is an experienced partner who knows Pontefract well.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out, with seconds at five and six starts back too, he arrives with genuine claims and today's trip and going already covered. A flatter spell in between - fourth twice and an eighth - is the one blot on his record.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Lightly-framed eight-year-old with a terrific strike rate (two wins, three places in last five on similar going) wearing a hood; a genuine hold-up type whose true position will be at the rear despite being mapped to midfield due to the redistribution of pace — the STYLE_FIT discount applies and their chance hinges on a stronger pace than Goyard is likely to supply.
runners_data.comment: A winner last time out and three times successful in her last six starts, she boasts a big strike-rate for a runner rated bottom of this five-runner field. Today's trip and going are already covered, though two sixth-place efforts show she can find one too many.

races.paceDynamic: Goyard is the lone confirmed front-runner in a five-strong field and, with no genuine speed rivals to challenge them for the lead, should secure a comfortable, uncontested gallop down the Pontefract straight on Good to Firm ground. The Good Biscuit is also rated as prominent but is more of a pace-follower than a pace-maker, meaning Goyard can dictate terms at whatever tempo they choose. With hold-up horses Trilby and Bell Shot sitting deepest, and Iris Dancer redistributed to midfield despite being a true hold-up type, the race is set up as a lone-leader scenario with chasers trying to close from behind. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and front-runners who can control the tempo, rather than horses waiting for a late injection of pace that may never come at a modest gallop — hold-up horses face a stiffer task unless the pace is genuinely strong.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Goyard Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard dictates a comfortable solo lead and the chasers cannot close the gap on Good to Firm ground.
scenarios.body: Goyard sets the fractions from the front without any pressure, rationing their effort and arriving at the final furlong with reserves intact; the hold-up horses are too far back to reel them in under a modest pace. Prominent types and front-runners are the clear beneficiaries of this lone-leader shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Chasers Reel In Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Goyard's early gallop proves faster than sustainable and The Good Biscuit leads the pursuit.
scenarios.body: Goyard's effort over 6f — a furlong beyond their best winning trip of 5f — catches up with them in the final stages, leaving The Good Biscuit and any close traveller to mop up late. Prominent types following the pace are best placed to capitalise as the leader ties up.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and the hold-up runners get a tow into the race off genuine fractions.
scenarios.body: Trilby and Bell Shot, both proven over 6f on Good ground, stay widest or closest to the action and produce a strong late surge if the pace proves quicker than expected. This scenario is discounted because both Iris Dancer and Trilby are true hold-up types who need a strong pace that a lone, uncontested front-runner is unlikely to supply.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Disrupted Start Scrambles Order
scenarios.trigger: If there is a slow break or interference that reshuffles positions and neutralises Goyard's tactical advantage.
scenarios.body: A poor early exchange could bring all runners into a bunched, tactical race where form and weight-carrying ability become decisive rather than pace control. Lower probability as nothing in the data points to this outcome and small fields at Pontefract rarely produce chaotic breaks.

watchPoints.text: Goyard's 6f stamina is the pivotal question — watch for any signs of shortening stride in the final furlong, as a lone front-runner who ties up hands the race to The Good Biscuit and anyone else in close attendance.

Iris Dancer has strong winning form on Good over 6f but is a true hold-up type in a race where the pace may not be strong enough to create a gap — watch whether Rowan Scott elects to track closer than usual to compensate.

Bell Shot's five most recent races have all been over 7f or further; the sharp return to 6f on what is riding Good to Firm at Pontefract could find them coming up short for speed in the dash to the line.
Trilby ran just one day ago — monitor any market drift or support that suggests connections are confident the quick turnaround has left them fresh rather than fatigued.

With only five runners and a lone front-runner, draw and early positioning may be unusually significant — watch the early stall break to see whether The Good Biscuit can sit directly behind Goyard rather than being outpaced off the bend.
